title: Dynamic Commands and Dispatch knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under “Dynamic Commands and Dispatch”?
questions.explanation: The supplied Bash.pdf curriculum lists “Selecting commands from validated options” under lesson 147, “Dynamic Commands and Dispatch”. Review the topic in the lesson content to connect the term with its practical use.

questions.prompt: Which approach is the strongest default when applying “Dynamic Commands and Dispatch”?
options: Evaluate constructed user-controlled strings as shell commands to reduce parsing code.
Skip version checks because all common environments provide the same Bash features.
Document the minimum Bash version and use complex features only when their behavior is tested.
Assume that a working happy-path example proves correctness for every input.
questions.answer_key: Document the minimum Bash version and use complex features only when their behavior is tested.
questions.explanation: Document the minimum Bash version and use complex features only when their behavior is tested. This approach keeps assumptions visible and makes results verifiable.

questions.prompt: Which practice best prevents a common reliability or maintenance error related to “Dynamic Commands and Dispatch”?
options: Assume the command behaves the same across all versions and operating systems.
Skip invalid inputs because the example uses trusted sample data.
Treat one successful output as proof that the workflow is safe in production.
Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation.
questions.answer_key: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation.
questions.explanation: Use a small reproducible example, test an edge case, and record both the result and an important limitation. The appropriate checks depend on the target environment and should be reviewed before publishing a script.
